bracket: [Textbook misprint in the answer key: it prints \(Q = m\!\left({}^{56}_{26}\text{Fe}\right) - 2m\!\left({}^{28}_{13}\text{Al}\right) = 26.90\,\text{MeV}\), dropping the minus sign from its own result. The magnitude and the verdict are both right — only the sign is missing — and the key refutes itself twice over. Its own printed expression, evaluated with the stem's own data, gives \(55.93494 - 2(27.98191) = -0.028881\,\text{u}\), i.e. \(-26.90\,\text{MeV}\); and its own conclusion \(\text{'not possible'}\) requires \(Q < 0\), since a \(Q\) of \(+26.90\,\text{MeV}\) would be exothermic and therefore possible. The negative value is also the physically expected one: \({}^{56}_{26}\text{Fe}\) sits at the peak of the binding-energy-per-nucleon curve, so splitting it must cost energy rather than release it.]
